headline: Sibol Wins Asian Games Honor of Kings Bronze After Loss to China
seoTitle: Sibol Wins Asian Games Honor of Kings Bronze | FMB News
seoDescription: The Philippines won bronze in Honor of Kings at the 2026 Asian Games after an official 0–2 semifinal loss to China at Aichi Sky Expo.
deck: The Philippine team fell 0–2 to China in the official semifinal scorecard, ending its Honor of Kings campaign with bronze.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Philippines won bronze in the Honor of Kings event at the 2026 Asian Games after losing 0–2 to China in the semifinal at Aichi Sky Expo Hall D on Monday.
The official Aichi-Nagoya results service marked the September 28 semifinal result as official. China won both sets and advanced to the gold-medal match.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Sibol reached the semifinals after sweeping South Korea 2–0 in the quarterfinals on September 27, a result that had already assured the team of at least a bronze medal.

GMA News reported the completed semifinal result and the bronze medal. The official scorecard identifies the competing entries as the Philippines and the People's Republic of China and records a 0–2 final score.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The result adds another medal to the Philippines' Asian Games campaign and another podium finish for the national esports program.
It follows the Philippines' bronze in Pokémon UNITE, extending the country's medal presence across more than one esports title at the Games.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: China advanced to face Malaysia in the Honor of Kings gold-medal match. The Philippine team's event is complete.
The overall Philippine medal tally may continue to change as other events on the September 28 program conclude.

verificationNotes: The official Aichi-Nagoya 2026 results service records the Philippines losing 0–2 to China in the September 28 Honor of Kings semifinal and marks the result official.
GMA News independently reports that the semifinal loss left Sibol with the bronze medal.
Philstar.com independently reported the Philippines' 2–0 quarterfinal win over South Korea and that the victory guaranteed at least bronze before the semifinal.
The article does not reuse event imagery whose publication rights are not independently verified.
The 1200-by-675 FMB News editorial fallback is used and is explicitly identified as a non-documentary visual that does not depict the match.
A dedicated Context section separates the completed official scorecard from the earlier quarterfinal qualification.
